20261014-hackathon-problem-statement-fe-b587

Operators open the shared workspace link directly to the yard overview, then move into yard records to sync procurement, review exceptions, map lots and pens, and record weights. Feed management handles inventory, rations, plans, and actual deliveries; the Insights hub brings together operational reports, the filtered Feed-to-Gain comparison, exports, and the project presentation.

Yard overviewYardFeed managementInsights
Serves 4 requirements
  • REQ-1 The Feedlot web app shall provide a shared workspace from its app link without a sign-in screen and present the same operational and financial controls to all users without role-specific permission choices.
  • REQ-24 The Feedlot web app shall provide an operational dashboard showing active lots and pens, animals per lot and pen, feed inventory status, ration usage, daily bunk rate per pen, planned versus actual feed, total feed consumed, total feed cost, starting and current weight, total weight gain, average daily gain, feed-to-gain ratio, feed cost per unit of gain, energy consumed, and best- and worst-performing lots.
  • REQ-28 The Feedlot web app shall provide a yard-level summary showing aggregate total head, average ADG, average cost of gain, and total feed cost across active lots.
  • REQ-29 The Feedlot web app shall provide representative mock operational data and a project presentation page containing the proposed solution, architecture diagrams, demo walkthrough, coding prompts, testing and validation overview, challenges, production-readiness assessment, and go-to-market strategy and analysis.

Yard overviewYardFeed managementInsights
Serves 11 requirements
  • REQ-2 When an operator starts a mock procurement synchronization, the Feedlot web app shall request PO and receiving records from the mock source adapter and display the returned procurement and receiving fields.
  • REQ-3 The Feedlot web app shall let users map one PO line to one or multiple lots and map those lots to pens while showing PO-line traceability, pen ID, capacity, and returned current animal count.
  • REQ-4 When an import result identifies duplicate, changed, or conflicting source records, the Feedlot web app shall display the affected records, returned conflict status and mapping information, and a review action.
  • REQ-5 When lifecycle forecast data is returned, the Feedlot web app shall display each lot's target weight and projected market or ship date, leaving the projected-date field empty when ADG is zero or negative.
  • REQ-6 The Feedlot web app shall display a lot-specific target and gain assumption when available and use the configured yard target when procurement does not supply a target.
  • REQ-7 The Feedlot web app shall display the configured yard-level target weight for all lots.
  • REQ-18 The Feedlot web app shall let users record lot weight measurements with measurement date, number of animals weighed, average animal weight, and notes; calculate total measured weight as average weight multiplied by number weighed; and provide no independent total-weight entry field.
  • REQ-19 The Feedlot web app shall display each lot's weight measurement history as a time-ordered list of dated records including average weight, number weighed, total measured weight, weight gain since the prior measurement, and notes when returned.
  • REQ-20 When a user edits or voids a saved feeding or weight record, the Feedlot web app shall display returned revised balances and metrics while retaining the original record in the record history.
  • REQ-22 The Feedlot web app shall display returned lot feed-to-gain metrics for days on feed, total weight gain, average daily gain, total feed consumed, feed conversion ratio, feed cost per unit of weight gain, and projected ship date, using recorded feed costs only for feed cost per unit of gain.
  • REQ-23 When a feeding or weight event is saved and updated metrics or predictive insights are returned, the Feedlot web app shall refresh the displayed lot metrics and show returned feeding-adjustment or sale-timing suggestions.

New ration

Set the ingredient mix and animal range. The returned ration cost uses current inventory unit-cost snapshots.

Percentages must total 100%; quantities are calculated in pounds.

Plan or record a pen feeding

Plans return quantity, cost and expected energy. Actual deliveries decrement stock by delivered pounds and retain ingredient cost snapshots.

Returned plan quantity is rate × the selected pen head count.
The returned inventory decrement is based on delivered quantity.

Serves 12 requirements
  • REQ-8 The Feedlot web app shall let users view and enter feed inventory items and display their category, available quantity, unit, unit cost, dry-matter percentage, energy value, storage location, and opening, received, consumed, and closing stock values.
  • REQ-9 When the inventory service refuses a stock movement that would make available inventory negative, the Feedlot web app shall show the returned shortage and refusal message and leave the movement visibly unsaved for correction.
  • REQ-10 The Feedlot web app shall let users configure a wastage ratio and display ingredient balance and shortage forecasts for daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, bi-annual, and annual horizons using dated feeding-plan demand and wastage-adjusted estimated consumption.
  • REQ-11 The Feedlot web app shall let users create and view rations with a name, type, ingredient quantities or as-fed proportions, dry-matter percentage, energy value, intended animal type or weight range, and returned calculated cost per pound.
  • REQ-12 The Feedlot web app shall provide a ration comparison view showing returned ration costs and associated lot performance or cost-of-gain values, and identify the mix with the lowest returned cost of gain when that comparison value is available.
  • REQ-13 Where inventory or ration screens display ton-denominated prices, the Feedlot web app shall display the equivalent per-pound price in the configured currency and display calculation quantities in pounds.
  • REQ-14 The Feedlot web app shall let users generate a dated pen feeding plan from a selected ration, per-animal daily bunk rate, pen animal count, date, and planned feeding time, and display the returned planned quantity, quantity per animal, total feed cost, expected energy intake, and plan status.
  • REQ-15 When a feeding plan is for a pen containing multiple lots, the Feedlot web app shall require a planned quantity allocation for every lot and flag allocations that do not reconcile with the plan total.
  • REQ-16 When a user saves an actual feeding event, the Feedlot web app shall display the returned planned quantity, actual delivered quantity, actual-minus-planned variance, feed cost, energy value, inventory decrement based on delivered quantity, feeding status, lot allocation, and the ingredient unit-cost snapshot recorded at save time.
  • REQ-17 When an actual feeding activity differs from its plan, the Feedlot web app shall show the planned-versus-actual variance and provide an action to adjust a future feeding plan.
  • REQ-20 When a user edits or voids a saved feeding or weight record, the Feedlot web app shall display returned revised balances and metrics while retaining the original record in the record history.
  • REQ-23 When a feeding or weight event is saved and updated metrics or predictive insights are returned, the Feedlot web app shall refresh the displayed lot metrics and show returned feeding-adjustment or sale-timing suggestions.

Project presentation

Proposed solution

One traceable workspace connects lot and pen records, ration plans, feed deliveries, weights and inventory. Daily plan-versus-actual and Feed-to-Gain results help staff correct the next bunk or buying decision.

Architecture & data flow

Flow: Responsive browser → web API → operational database (lots, pens, rations, deliveries, weights) → report service → CSV/PDF. Imports and edits write an audit log; yard roles scope access.

Demo walkthrough

Open the yard overview; sync procurement and review pen exceptions; compare ADG, FCR and cost of gain for 01–30 Mar; export CSV or PDF for the selected scope; review validation and readiness.

Coding prompts

Prompt A: Add date, lot, breed, sex and pen filters; calculate ADG, FCR and USD/kg gain from traceable weights and deliveries. Prompt B: export the exact filtered results to CSV/PDF and add scope-parity tests.

Testing & validation

Check ADG, FCR and cost of gain against hand-calculated lots; reconcile planned feed, deliveries and inventory; verify exports match filtered rows. Validate empty scopes, stale syncs, permissions and phone, tablet and desktop layouts.

Challenges

Delayed scale tickets, duplicate feed slips, ration-name drift and missing weigh-ins can skew results. Reconcile imports by source ID, flag missing or implausible values, retain the last good report and audit corrections.

Production readiness

Readiness: yard-scoped roles, audit logs, encrypted data, restore drills, export limits, error monitoring and feed-sync retries. Pilot gate: reconciled weights and stock, reviewed access, support and rollback documented.

Go-to-market analysis

Target independent yards with 150–2,000 head. Lead with feed variance and cost-of-gain proof; offer a 30-day pilot, then annual per-head pricing. Onboard through feed consultants and co-ops. Track active pens, variance improvement and…

Architecture & data flow

Flow: Responsive browser → web API → operational database (lots, pens, rations, deliveries, weights) → report service → CSV/PDF. Imports and edits write an audit log; yard roles scope access.

Demo walkthrough

Open the yard overview; sync procurement and review pen exceptions; compare ADG, FCR and cost of gain for 01–30 Mar; export CSV or PDF for the selected scope; review validation and readiness.

Coding prompts

Prompt A: Add date, lot, breed, sex and pen filters; calculate ADG, FCR and USD/kg gain from traceable weights and deliveries. Prompt B: export the exact filtered results to CSV/PDF and add scope-parity tests.

Testing & validation

Check ADG, FCR and cost of gain against hand-calculated lots; reconcile planned feed, deliveries and inventory; verify exports match filtered rows. Validate empty scopes, stale syncs, permissions and phone, tablet and desktop layouts.

Challenges

Delayed scale tickets, duplicate feed slips, ration-name drift and missing weigh-ins can skew results. Reconcile imports by source ID, flag missing or implausible values, retain the last good report and audit corrections.

Production readiness

Readiness: yard-scoped roles, audit logs, encrypted data, restore drills, export limits, error monitoring and feed-sync retries. Pilot gate: reconciled weights and stock, reviewed access, support and rollback documented.

Go-to-market analysis

Target independent yards with 150–2,000 head. Lead with feed variance and cost-of-gain proof; offer a 30-day pilot, then annual per-head pricing. Onboard through feed consultants and co-ops. Track active pens, variance improvement and…

Yard overviewYardFeed managementInsights
Serves 4 requirements
  • REQ-25 The Feedlot web app shall provide operational report views identifying the highest-feed-consuming pen, best feed-to-gain lot, highest-ADG lot, most-used ration, plan-versus-actual alignment, overfed or underfed pens, remaining inventory, and feed cost per unit of weight gain.
  • REQ-26 The Feedlot web app shall provide a dedicated Feed-to-Gain report with date-range, lot, breed, sex, and pen filters to compare ADG, FCR, and cost of gain across lots.
  • REQ-27 When a user exports the Feed-to-Gain report, the Feedlot web app shall provide CSV and PDF files containing the report results for the selected filter scope.
  • REQ-29 The Feedlot web app shall provide representative mock operational data and a project presentation page containing the proposed solution, architecture diagrams, demo walkthrough, coding prompts, testing and validation overview, challenges, production-readiness assessment, and go-to-market strategy and analysis.
